How Rico works.

01

Reads your channels

Invite Rico in. It spots the moments where someone commits to doing something.

02

Captures commitments

Owner, deadline, and source are captured automatically. Rico asks once if anything needs clarification, and a single click fixes it.

03

Keeps work moving

Everyone can see what's in motion, what's blocked, and what's overdue. Rico only steps in when something needs an owner, a deadline, or a follow-up.

Every project has a living record.

Not meeting notes. Not another task list. Just the complete history of decisions, conversations, and commitments in one place.

Ask Rico a question and it answers from your Slack history, with sources attached.

Emily 9:14 AM
What did we decide about the pricing rollout?
Rico APP 8:57 AM
We agreed to launch Pro first, then Enterprise two weeks later, once billing is complete.
Yesterday · GTM planningMonday · Pricing reviewLast week · Launch thread
Answered from your own history, sources attached

The hard part isn't the work. It's keeping track of it.

Commitments get made in meetings, in Slack, in email, in Jira tickets that go stale. Knowing who's overloaded, or whether a milestone is on track, usually means asking around.
